summary: @servicetitan/time-zones 3.8.2 preinstall downloads Bun runtime to execute obfuscated bundle
details: The package is published as a React/MobX time-zone UI component library but its package.json declares scripts.preinstall = "node setup.mjs". setup.mjs is obfuscated (obfuscator.io-style _0xXXXX identifiers and per-call string-map decoy objects) and, at npm install time, downloads the Bun runtime from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/<platform>.zip, extracts it, chmods it 0o755, and calls execFileSync(bunPath, [path.join(D, "math_init.js")], { stdio: "inherit" }). If Bun is already on PATH the download step is skipped and the same file is executed directly. math_init.js is a 727 KB Bun-compiled bundle (`// @bun @bun-cjs`) whose contents are hidden behind a shuffled string-array cipher (WV8StW rotator over the n7gIxM array), a form that resists Node-based static and dynamic analysis. package.json declares "files": ["dist", "src"], yet math_init.js and setup.mjs sit at the tarball root outside both directories, indicating the payload was injected outside the maintainer's normal publish flow. A UI time-zone library has no legitimate reason to fetch an alternate JavaScript runtime at install time and use it to run an opaque bundled payload; the runtime substitution routes execution around Node-based supply-chain scanners. The precise post-execution behavior of math_init.js is not readable from the shipped form, but installing this version causes attacker-authored code to run under Bun on the installer's machine at npm install time.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
